description:
Give the captured mutation base one memoised parse of its image's declarations and make the mutation derivations reuse it, so a mutation parses each captured image's configuration, gates and rules at most once.

## Background

- `MutationBase` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:863-868`) holds only the captured image and its issues, and `capture_mutation_base` (`validate.rs:211-227`) returns it. Every consumer that needs configuration, gates or rules parses the image again through `declarations_from_image` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:411`) or `assemble_config` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/materialize.rs:67`).
- `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2769`) parses its session image twice in one attempt: for the lease mode and precheck plan (`mod.rs:2913`) and again before deriving the transition (`mod.rs:3104`). Its preflight image is a separate capture with its own parse (`mod.rs:2810`), which stays.
- Other base readers parse the base image themselves: `publish_issue_creation` (`mod.rs:2385`, parse at `:2412`), `publish_captured_field_update` (`mod.rs:2599`, parse at `:2630`), `batch_create_from_json` (`crates/jit/src/commands/batch_create.rs:312-317`) and the bulk derivation's base in `crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`.
- Parsing eagerly inside `capture_mutation_base` would change behaviour: the dependency edit (`publish_captured_dependency_mutation`, `crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:264`, parse at `:304`) reads only `config.toml` today and would start failing on an unparseable `rules.toml`. A parse on first use keeps every mutation's failure set as it is.
- Struct patterns over `MutationBase` without `..` stop compiling when a field is added: `dependency.rs:290,379`, `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:640`, `crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:367`, `mod.rs:2619,2896` and the test helper `capture_precheck_plan` (`mod.rs:3646-3671`, pattern at `:3655`).
- Deletion: `IssueOps::delete_issue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:612-662`) parses the base image with `assemble_config` (`:647`), then `derive_issue_deletion` (`issue.rs:67-76`) parses the same image with `declarations_from_image` and `assemble_config` again (`:75-76`), three parses per attempt. The preflight parse (`:630`) reads a different capture and stays.
- Dependency edits: `publish_captured_dependency_removal` (`dependency.rs:361`) parses with both functions (`:384-385`); `publish_captured_dependency_mutation` (`:264`) parses the base with `assemble_config` (`:304`).
- `apply_gate_preset` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:1256`) parses its session image with `assemble_config` (`:1294`), parses `gates.toml` through `captured_gate_registry` (`:365`), and parses everything again with `declarations_from_image` (`:1322`). `publish_gate_registry_mutation` (`gate.rs:1012`) parses `gates.toml` with `parse_gate_registry` (`:1065`) and again inside `declarations_from_image` (`:1071`).
- `project_render` (`crates/jit/src/commands/project.rs:115`) parses the final image with `declarations_from_image` (`:159`) after its discovery round parsed it with `assemble_config` (`:142`).
- `derive_captured_template_apply` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:330-344`) parses configuration through `template_config_from_image` (`:338`, `:547`), `gates.toml` through its gate registry parse (`:683`), and both again through `template_declarations_from_image` (`:344`, `:574`).
- The configuration assembler is the only path from bytes to `JitConfig` (`configuration-assembly`), and `apply_gate_preset` and `derive_captured_template_apply` read presets through the public gate-preset catalog (`gate-preset-catalog`).
- The lease checks in the dependency edits and the bulk path, the precheck evidence capture in the lifecycle block (`gate-evidence-capture`), and the content-format reads in `publish_issue_creation` are edited upstream; this task takes them as those changes leave them.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `MutationBase::declarations()` returns the `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` of the base image, parsed by one `declarations_from_image` call on first use and returned from that parse on every later call for the same base.
- [hard] REQ-02: `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation`, `publish_issue_creation`, `publish_captured_field_update`, `batch_create_from_json`, the bulk derivation, `delete_issue`, `derive_issue_deletion`, `publish_captured_dependency_mutation` and `publish_captured_dependency_removal` read configuration, gates and rules of the base image only through `MutationBase::declarations()`; none calls `declarations_from_image` or `assemble_config` on the base image, and `derive_issue_deletion` receives the declarations instead of parsing.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test shows that two calls to `MutationBase::declarations()` on one base return the same parsed value (pointer-equal) and that a base whose `gates.toml` is unparseable returns the parse error from each call.
- [hard] REQ-04: `apply_gate_preset`, `publish_gate_registry_mutation`, `project_render` and `derive_captured_template_apply` parse their final captured image's declarations with one call and take configuration and the gate registry from that result.
- [hard] REQ-05: The deletion, dependency, gate preset, gate registry, projection render, template application, lifecycle, issue creation, field update, batch create and bulk update suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged: a mutation fails on an unparseable declaration exactly when it consulted that declaration before.
- The preflight capture is a different image and keeps its own single parse.
- Discovery rounds that read configuration to enumerate a capture closure (`project.rs:142`, `gate.rs:1048`, `capture_gate_preset_image` at `gate.rs:292-321`) parse images that are still growing. Each round's image differs from the final one, so "once per captured image" holds; they are outside this change.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Mutation bases carry their parsed declarations and derivations reuse them
